title: Generative models, graphical models and dependence
summary: Knowledge as generative models; directed graphical models and their factorisation; causal versus statistical dependence; screening off and explaining away; intervention versus observation; sampling as a way of interrogating a model.

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is OCW lectures 9 and 10 (graphical models and Bayes nets; Bayes-net semantics, explaining away, sampling) and the web book's chapters Generative models, Causal and statistical dependence and Conditional dependence.

preparation.description: Read OCW lecture 9 (Graphical Models and Bayes Nets) and lecture 10 (Bayes-net semantics, explaining away, sampling possible worlds; the file is oct_12_2004_fin.pdf).

Read the web book's Generative models (models, simulation and degrees of belief; the rules of probability), Causal and statistical dependence, and Conditional dependence (screening off, explaining away, blickets). Reference-only: read on the book's site.
